Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted. On state-changing operations this status may also carry `code: csrf_token_invalid` (SR-041; see `CsrfTokenInvalid`). An enrolment-only session gets `code: mfa_enrollment_required` from every operation outside its allow-list (see the Enrolment-only session section of `info.description`). A session that holds a view-as context gets `code: view_as_read_only` from every state-changing operation outside the viewer's own ones, and `code: view_as_expired` from every operation outside them once the server has ended the context (see the View-as session section of `info.description`). Both honour the C-2.6 carve-out below: while viewing, the writes it names and engaging the kill switch on an account set are not refused (see the View-as session section), and leaving view-as is one call that nothing refuses. `detail` never echoes token or cookie values. On a dangerous operation it may carry `code: step_up_required`: that body is a step-up challenge for the refused request (`challenge_id`, `challenge_expires_at`, `action_class`, `action_summary`, `target`; see `POST /auth/step-up`, #2304). On an order submit or amend it may also be the order-entry gate's refusal: `code: trading_disabled` with a `reason` member (`TradingDisabledProblem`, #837 Q5). `reason` appears on gate refusals only: the B18 kill switch (FREEZE) and the live-not-enabled refusal are separate synchronous checks ahead of the gate, and they return `trading_disabled` without a `reason`. Like the gate, they run after authentication, RBAC and account-scope resolution, and the C-2.6 carve-out binds every synchronous refusal, not just the gate: attaching a missing native SL, tightening a stop or re-arming a protective trigger is never refused. `createApiKey` and `testApiKey` answer `code: kek_unavailable` while the credential key (KEK) is unavailable (ADR-0009 Amendment 1).

Drawing.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

updated_at.description: Concurrency token (also the `ETag`). Always exactly 6 fractional digits plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`) and strictly increasing on every write. Echo it exactly as received; never re-serialise it through a client date type.

if_match.description: `updated_at` of the version being deleted: echo it exactly as received (6 fractional digits plus `Z`); never re-serialise it through a client date type. A token that does not match is a 422 on `operations.N.if_match`.

operations.description: Applied in order. More than 200 items is `413 payload_too_large`.

DrawingBatchResult.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

if_match.description: `updated_at` of the version being replaced: echo it exactly as received (6 fractional digits plus `Z`); never re-serialise it through a client date type. A token that does not match is a 422 on `operations.N.if_match`.

DrawingGeometry.description:
Chart-space geometry (time + price, never pixels). Per-tool point counts and key rules: see `DrawingTool`.

Observable validation (all `422 validation_failed` unless stated): JSON nesting depth must
be at most 16; `NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected; a string that cannot be encoded as UTF-8
(a lone surrogate) is rule `invalid_unicode`. `text` is sanitised on write, before the length
check: U+0000-U+001F except LF (U+000A, kept in `text` only), U+007F-U+009F, U+2028, U+2029,
U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 are removed; nothing else is altered
(no trim, no normalisation). Text that is empty after sanitising is rule `text_required`.
Reads return the sanitised text, so it may differ from what was sent.

levels.description: Fibonacci levels (fib tools only): unique finite numbers; a duplicate is rule `duplicate_level`. Non-zero items must have |x| ≥ 1e-6 (`number_out_of_range`).

items.description: A non-zero number must have |x| ≥ 1e-6 (`number_out_of_range`); zero is allowed. `-0.0` is stored as `0.0`.

text.description: Text content (`text` and `callout` only), 1..1000 code points after control-character stripping (LF is kept).

DrawingInput.description:
Write payload. Strings are sanitised on write exactly as described on `DrawingGeometry`
(for `label` LF is removed too; an empty result is rule `string_too_short`), and a read
returns the sanitised value. The nesting-depth, `NaN`/`Infinity` and `invalid_unicode`
rules there apply to the whole body.

label.description: Display label, 1..120 code points after control-character stripping.

layout_id.description: Layout scope. A non-null value must be one of the caller's live layouts, else 422 rule `layout_not_found`; every non-null value is refused until layouts ship (E15-T01).

style.description: Optional; omitted means no style overrides (stored as `{}`, returned as `{}`).

symbol.description: Bybit USDT linear perpetual symbol, at most 20 characters (the DB symbol_code domain).

p.description: Chart-space price coordinate as a decimal string; may be negative. Stored and returned verbatim, never converted to a float.

t.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with `Z`, at most millisecond precision, years 2000-2099.

fill_opacity.description: A non-zero number must have |x| ≥ 1e-6 (`number_out_of_range`); zero is allowed. `-0.0` is stored as `0.0`.

DrawingTool.description:
Drawing tool. **Open-ended for readers:** clients must tolerate values they do not know, so
adding a tool is an additive change (C-6.3). Writers must send one of the listed values.

Required point count per tool (`geometry.points`):

- exactly 1: `horizontal_line`, `vertical_line`, `text`, `anchored_vwap`
- exactly 2: `trendline`, `ray`, `extended_line`, `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `fib_retracement`,
  `fib_timezone`, `gann_fan`, `arrow`, `callout`, `measure`, `price_range`, `date_range`
- exactly 3: `parallel_channel`, `triangle`, `fib_extension`, `pitchfork`, `long_position`,
  `short_position`
- 2..500: `brush`; 2..100: `polyline`

Tool-specific `geometry` keys (any other combination is `422` rule `property_not_allowed_for_tool`):
`text` is required for `text` and `callout` (rule `text_required`) and forbidden elsewhere;
`levels` only for `fib_retracement`, `fib_extension`, `fib_timezone`; `bands` only for
`anchored_vwap`; `extend_left` / `extend_right` are allowed on every tool.
A horizontal ray is a `horizontal_line` with `extend_left: false` and `extend_right: true`.

Layout.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

updated_at.description: Concurrency token (also the `ETag`) of the whole layout aggregate, panes included: every write changes it, including a pane-only change and a default switch made by another layout. Always exactly 6 fractional digits plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`) and strictly increasing. Echo it exactly as received; never re-serialise it through a client date type.

slot.description: `slot_index` of a pane in the same layout.

LayoutGridPreset.description:
Named grid (`lay_preset`, `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1) or `custom`. A named preset stores
only its name and fixed cell proportions: `grid_spec` is `null`, and a pane's `slot_index`
is its cell in row-major reading order (a slot beyond the preset's cells is placed by the
client, e.g. floating). Any other arrangement, including a named grid whose divider was
dragged, is saved as `custom` with its tree in `grid_spec`. **Open-ended for readers.**

LayoutGridSpec.description:
Dock tree of a `custom` layout (`row` / `column` / `tabset` / `leaf`), checked at the API
boundary (`422`, field paths under `grid_spec`): depth at most 6 counting the root as 1
(rule `tree_too_deep`); at most 64 nodes and at most 16 leaves (rule `tree_too_large`);
every leaf names the `slot_index` of a pane in the same body (rule `unknown_slot`) and no
slot appears twice (rule `duplicate_leaf`), so the leaf cap also follows from `panes` having
at most 16 entries; a split's `sizes` has one entry per child (rule `sizes_mismatch`), each
in (0, 1], summing to 1 within 1e-6 (rule `sizes_sum`); a tabset's `active` indexes one of
its children (rule `active_out_of_range`). Panes that no leaf names are kept (floating or
minimised, placed by the client).

LayoutGridSplit.description: `row` lays children out left to right, `column` top to bottom; `sizes` are fractions of the container.

active.description: Index of the visible tab in `children`.

LayoutInput.description: Writable layout fields plus the complete pane set. `PUT` is a full replacement: an omitted field takes its default, an explicit `null` on a non-nullable field is refused, and the stored panes are replaced. Observable validation (depth, `NaN`/`Infinity`, `invalid_unicode`, `name` sanitising and rules) is as on `WorkspaceInput`.

crosshair_sync.description: Layout default for crosshair sync between panes of one sync group.

grid_spec.description: Required when `grid_preset` is `custom`, otherwise `null` or omitted.

hotkey_slot.description: `Ctrl+1..9` binding; unique among the workspace's live layouts (`409 conflict`, rule `hotkey_slot_taken`).

is_default.description: At most one live default per workspace; `true` clears the previous default in the same transaction.

name.description: At most 40 characters as sent, at least 1 after sanitising, as for workspace names. Unique per workspace, case-insensitive, among live layouts (`409 conflict`, rule `name_taken`).

panes.description: In any order: panes are keyed by `slot_index`, and responses sort by it.

LayoutPane.description: Stored pane (response object). Panes have no id of their own: they are addressed by `slot_index` and replaced as a set. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

chart_template_id.description: Chart template reference. Every non-null value is refused (`422` rule `chart_template_not_found`) until `chart_templates` ships; then it must name a template the caller may use.

indicator_preset_ids.description: Indicator preset references; omitted means `[]`. A non-empty list is refused (`422` rule `indicator_preset_not_found`) until `indicator_presets` ships (E13-T03); then every id must name a preset the caller may use.

interval_code.description: Bar series of a market pane; `null` for panes without one.

symbol.description: Bound symbol, market panes only: a Bybit USDT linear perpetual symbol of at most 20 characters (the DB `symbol_code` domain). It is not checked against the instrument catalogue. A non-null symbol on a live layout counts as chart-open for auto-recording.

LayoutPreset.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3); the embedded `layout` is a closed `LayoutInput`.

id.description: Stable for the life of the catalogue entry.

is_builtin.description: Always `true`: the catalogue is static. User-saved presets are layouts with a `hotkey_slot`.

OrderEntryRefusalReason.description: Why the shared order-entry gate refused an order (#837 Q5; E42-T03 and E27-T04). The server's set is closed and listed in `24-internal-schemas.md` 8.10. **Open-ended for readers:** clients must tolerate values they do not know, so adding a reason is an additive change (C-6.3).

count.description: Items in this page (not the total, which is never computed for unbounded sets).

total.description: Present only where a cheap exact count exists.

PaneConfig.description:
Per-pane view state with no column of its own, so a pane cannot become a blob store: closed
(unknown keys are refused, C-6.3; later stories add keys additively), at most 4096 bytes of
canonical compact UTF-8 JSON measured after sanitising (`422` rule `pane_config_too_large`),
and never holds credentials, account ids or user ids. Omitted means `{}`.

settings.description: Kind-specific flat settings (for example DOM depth, tape filters, CVD anchor, visible range), at most 32 keys. Every key must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$` (`422` rule `invalid_setting_key`); the server enforces this because generators cannot express key patterns. Numbers keep their kind (`1` stays `1`, `1.0` stays `1.0`). Omitted means `{}`.

sync_group.description: Cross-pane sync group (SCR-023); `null` or omitted means not synced. The axis defaults live on the layout (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`).

PaneIntervalCode.description: `<bar_type>:<param>`, exactly the `bar_type` and `param` of `/market/bars` (and of the WS topic `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`): `param` at most 24 characters, no leading zeros, and no trailing zeros in a `volume`/`delta` fraction, so each value has one spelling (`volume:0.5`, never `volume:0.50`), e.g. `time:1`, `time:D`, `tick:500`, `volume:0.5`, `renko:atr:14`, `pnf:10:3`. A `volume` or `delta` threshold must also be greater than 0 (`422` rule `interval_not_positive`).

PaneKind.description:
Pane kind (`lp_kind`, `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1). **Open-ended for readers:** clients
must tolerate values they do not know, so adding a kind is an additive change (C-6.3);
writers must send a listed value. Market panes (`chart`, `dom`, `tape`, `profile`, `cvd`,
`oi`, `deep_stats`, `regime`) may bind a `symbol` and `interval_code`; account panes
(`positions`, `journal`, `watchlist`, `alerts`) show many symbols and carry neither (rule
`property_not_allowed_for_kind`). A heatmap lives in the `dom` pane and orders in the
`positions` pane. A footprint is a `chart` pane; until chart templates exist (#2411) it is
marked by `pane_config.settings.footprint: true`, its options as further flat `footprint_*`
settings.

PaneSettingValue.description: A flat setting value: a string, an integer or other finite number (each keeps its kind), a boolean, `null`, or an array of at most 32 such strings, numbers or booleans; objects are not allowed. Strings, also inside arrays, are at most 256 characters as sent and are then sanitised like `WorkspaceInput.name` (the name strip set and trimming), except that an empty result is kept; a lone surrogate is rule `invalid_unicode`. Numbers, also inside arrays, lie within ±1e15, so they read back with the same kind and value. A non-zero number must have |x| ≥ 1e-15 (`number_out_of_range`); zero is allowed. `-0.0` is stored as `0.0`.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem detail. `code` mirrors the `x-error-codes` catalogue.

action_class.description: `step_up_required` only: the step-up class the refused request needs, one of the `action_class` values of `POST /auth/step-up`.

action_summary.description: `step_up_required` only: server-composed text naming exactly what the refused request would execute, built from the validated request (for example "Release kill switch, scope global"). It comes from a fixed per-route template. Request values appear in it only as validated enum values (bare) or as identifiers and server-resolved labels (quoted, each bounded by its own schema's `maxLength` or `format`), never as free text such as a `reason`, and never as key material, a password, a token, a TOTP or recovery code or any field the redaction deny-list names (C-12.6). A label alone never identifies an account or a rule, because labels can be renamed and need not be unique: each account named in it is followed by its `environment` and `exchange_uid` and each rule by the environments its scope includes, rendered bare (for example "Release kill switch, accounts 'demo-1' (demo, UID 1001234)" or "Arm rule 'Break-even' (live)"); an account's `environment` and `exchange_uid` never change after it is registered. Naming a rule this way is provisional: two rules can share a label and environments, and `rules:write` can rename a rule and change its scope, bindings and active version without a step-up, so the route slice of #2304 decides, before any rule template ships, whether a rule is also named by its bound accounts and whether the grant that arms it is also bound to its active version. Before a label is quoted, an apostrophe or a backslash in it is preceded by a backslash, and every character outside printable ASCII (U+0020 to U+007E) is written as `\u{`, its code point in upper-case hex zero-padded to four digits, and `}` (U+000A becomes `\u{000A}`, U+202E becomes `\u{202E}` and U+1F600 becomes `\u{1F600}`). That covers line breaks and other control characters, bidi embedding, override and isolate marks and look-alike quotation marks, so the quotes bound the label: the label `demo-1' (demo)` is quoted as `'demo-1\' (demo)'`. The step-up dialog shows it verbatim as its accessible description; a client never composes its own.

challenge_expires_at.description: `step_up_required` only: when the challenge expires, 5 minutes after issue (server clock). The client drops the held request then, without sending it.

challenge_id.description: `step_up_required` only: the challenge this refusal issued (#2304), a random UUIDv4 scoped to the issuing session, so a value from another session is unknown. One challenge is live per session; a newer refusal supersedes it. Send it as `challenge_id` to `POST /auth/step-up`; a step-up for a no-grace class must send it.

exchange.description: Present when the failure originated at Bybit.

instance.description: Correlation id, `urn:cv:req:{uuid}`; matches the `X-Request-Id` header and the audit entry.

revoked_reason.description: `session_revoked` only. `expired`: the 12 h absolute lifetime elapsed. `unlock_attempts_exceeded`: five consecutive wrong unlock passwords. `revoked`: any other revocation; the specific cause is not disclosed.

target.description: `step_up_required` only: the exact, case-sensitive text a typed confirmation must equal when the action asks for one (for example the account name), else null. Like `action_summary`, it is an identifier or a server-resolved label of the validated request, never free text or credential material. It is a label only when no other object of its kind that the caller can see has that label, compared case-insensitively, and the label is printable ASCII; otherwise it is the object's identifier.

Symbol.description: Bybit USDT linear perpetual symbol. v1 accepts USDT-quoted linear symbols only.

TradingDisabledProblem.description: The `403 trading_disabled` problem the order-entry gate returns when it refuses a submission or amend that opens or increases exposure, before any OMS work (C-2.21): the problem body plus the gate's `reason`. `detail` is human text and never carries an id or a secret. The gate runs after authentication, RBAC and account-scope resolution, so an account outside the caller's scope never reaches it and gets a `404`. Cancels, flatten and quantity-reducing or stop-tightening amends never pass through the gate. Attaching a missing native SL, tightening a stop, or re-arming a protective trigger is never gated; "trigger re-armed" means an exposure-increasing (entry) trigger. An amend with any risk-increasing component is gated.

Workspace.description: Response object. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

updated_at.description: Concurrency token (also the `ETag`) for the workspace metadata only; layout writes do not change it. Always exactly 6 fractional digits plus `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`) and strictly increasing on every write. Echo it exactly as received; never re-serialise it through a client date type.

WorkspaceBundle.description: Portable, credential-free export of presentation state only.

WorkspaceDetail.description: Response object: `Workspace` plus every live layout with its panes, so restore is one request per workspace. Readers must ignore unknown properties (C-6.3).

WorkspaceIconToken.description:
Design-system icon token for the workspace (a token name, never a URL or markup).
**Open-ended for readers:** clients must tolerate values they do not know, so adding a token
is an additive change (C-6.3). Writers must send a listed value; the server keeps the same
allow-list. `workspace.default` is the only token until the design-system icon registry
(CMP-019) publishes workspace icons.

WorkspaceInput.description:
Writable workspace fields. `PUT` is a full replacement: an omitted field takes its default,
and an explicit `null` is refused (`422`).

Observable validation (all `422 validation_failed`): JSON nesting depth must be at most 16;
`NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected; a string that cannot be encoded as UTF-8 (a lone
surrogate) is rule `invalid_unicode`. `name` is at most 40 characters as sent (rule
`string_too_long`), then sanitised: U+0000-U+001F, U+007F-U+009F, U+2028, U+2029, U+061C,
U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 are removed, then surrounding whitespace is
trimmed; nothing else is altered. Empty after sanitising is rule `string_too_short`. Reads
return the sanitised name.

is_default.description: At most one live default per user; `true` clears the previous default in the same transaction.

name.description: At most 40 characters as sent, at least 1 after sanitising (above), SCR-020. Unique per user, case-insensitive, among live workspaces (`409 conflict`, rule `name_taken`).

sort_order.description: Client-defined tab order; ties break by `id`.

get.description:
Drawings are stored in **chart space** (time + price), never pixels, so they survive
zoom, bar-type changes and DPI changes. Only the caller's live (not soft-deleted) drawings
are returned, ordered by `id` ascending, so a cursor walk is stable.

`symbol` is required. Without `layout_id` the result holds the caller's drawings on that
symbol in **both** scopes (symbol-global and layout-scoped). With `layout_id` the result is
narrowed to that layout, and the call returns `404` when the id is not one of the caller's
live layouts (always the case until layouts ship, E15-T01).

`limit` is 1..500 (default 100). `cursor` is opaque, bound to the `symbol`/`layout_id`
scope it was issued for and valid for one hour; a malformed, mismatched or expired cursor
returns `400 invalid_cursor`.

parameters.description: Narrow to one layout. Must be one of the caller's live layouts, otherwise 404.
parameters.name: layout_id

value.title: Pagination cursor is malformed or expired

400.description: Malformed request. For this operation `code: invalid_cursor` signals a malformed, scope-mismatched or expired `cursor`.

get.summary: List the caller's drawings for a symbol

post.description:
The server mints a UUIDv7 `id`. The body is limited to 64 KiB (`413 payload_too_large`).
A non-null `layout_id` must name one of the caller's live layouts, otherwise
`422` rule `layout_not_found` (every non-null value until layouts ship, E15-T01).
The `ETag` response header carries the `updated_at` token for later `If-Match` use.

`Idempotency-Key`: the same key with the same body replays the stored 2xx response with
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`.
Replay storage is best-effort and bounded; correctness never depends on it.
The replay cache is in memory and bounded: a retry after the entry was evicted, or after a
server restart, creates a **duplicate** drawing. Clients that need retry-safe creation
should use `batchUpsertDrawings` with a client-chosen `id` (a repeat is `409 id_unavailable`).

The chart engine batches drawing mutations during a drag with a 500 ms debounce, so a single
call carries all affected shapes.

Processing order: (1) the body is limited to 1 MiB and `operations` to 200 items, otherwise
`413 payload_too_large`, checked before per-operation validation; (2) the whole body is
validated (`422`, up to 20 field errors such as `operations.3.drawing.tool`; each `id` may
appear at most once per batch, else rule `duplicate_id`); (3) the operations are applied in
order inside **one transaction**. The first operation that cannot be applied rolls the
whole batch back and returns `409 conflict` with `errors[0] = {field: "operations.<i>", rule, message}`,
where `rule` is one of:

- `target_unavailable` — an `update`/`delete` target is missing, soft-deleted or owned by
  another user (indistinguishable by design);
- `version_conflict` — the operation's `if_match` is stale;
- `id_unavailable` — a `create` id is already used by any row of any owner in any state
  (an id stays unavailable until its row is purged, 90 days after deletion; re-create under a new id).

`create.id` is optional (client UUIDv7 recommended); `update` and `delete` require `if_match`,
the `updated_at` token of the version being replaced or removed. The result lists the
created, updated and deleted ids in operation order.

`Idempotency-Key` behaves as on `createDrawing`.

errors.message: The target drawing is not available.

value.title: Concurrent modification or state conflict

409.description: The batch was rolled back. `errors[0].field` names the failing operation and `rule` is `target_unavailable`, `version_conflict` or `id_unavailable`; a reused `Idempotency-Key` with a different body is `idempotency_key_reuse`.

post.summary: Create/update/delete many drawings in one call

delete.description:
Soft delete (the row is purged by retention later). No precondition. A drawing that is
missing, already deleted or owned by another user returns the same `404`.

put.description:
Full replacement. `symbol` and `tool` are immutable (`422` rule `immutable_field`). The body
is limited to 64 KiB (`413 payload_too_large`).

`If-Match` is optional: the quoted `updated_at` token (a `W/` prefix or the bare token is
also accepted). A stale or unparseable value returns `412 version_conflict`; when absent the
last write wins. A drawing that is missing, soft-deleted or owned by another user returns
the same `404`.

get.description:
Static built-in catalogue served from the code (no rows, nothing user-scoped). Each entry
carries a complete `LayoutInput` for `createLayout`, symbols left for the client to fill
("Keep current symbols", SCR-022). User-saved presets are layouts with a `hotkey_slot`
(`listLayouts`). Ids are stable and new entries are additive. Thumbnails are static client
assets keyed by `id`; the API never serves markup. `cursor` as on `listWorkspaces`.

400.description: Malformed request. For this operation `code: invalid_cursor` signals a malformed or expired `cursor`.

get.description:
The caller's live workspaces ordered by `sort_order`, then `id`. A user holds at most 32, so
the default page returns them all. `cursor` is opaque, bound to this listing and valid for
one hour; a malformed, foreign or expired cursor returns `400 invalid_cursor`.

400.description: Malformed request. For this operation `code: invalid_cursor` signals a malformed, foreign or expired `cursor`.

post.description:
The server mints a UUIDv7 `id`. `409 conflict`: rule `name_taken` (names are unique per
user, case-insensitive, among live workspaces), `limit_reached` (32 live workspaces) or
`concurrent_update` (a racing write; retry). `is_default: true` clears the previous default
in the same transaction (its token changes); `false` touches no other workspace, and a user
may have no default.

Bodies over 4 KiB are refused with `413` (`payload_too_large`). The `ETag` header carries
the `updated_at` token for `If-Match`. `Idempotency-Key` is accepted, never required
(`x-idempotency: optional`): the same key and request replay the stored 2xx response with
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`. The replay fingerprint covers the method, path and body, so
the same key with another request is `409 idempotency_key_reuse`. Replay storage is in
memory, best-effort and bounded; correctness never depends on it.

delete.description:
Soft delete in one transaction: the workspace, its live layouts and their drawings get the
same `deleted_at`; retention purges them later. Deleting the caller's **last** live
workspace is `409 conflict` with `errors[0].rule = last_workspace` ("You need at least one
workspace.", SCR-025), and nothing changes. Deleting the default leaves no default. No
precondition. Missing, already deleted or another user's: the same `404`. `Idempotency-Key`
as on `createWorkspace` (a replay returns the stored `204`).

value.detail: You need at least one workspace.

errors.message: You need at least one workspace.

value.title: Concurrent modification or state conflict

409.description: State conflict. For this operation `code: conflict` with `errors[0].rule = last_workspace` refuses deleting the caller's last live workspace; `code: idempotency_key_reuse` is the shared idempotency refusal.

delete.summary: Delete a workspace and its layouts

get.description:
Restore in one request: the workspace plus every live layout with all of its panes (layouts
by `id`, panes by `slot_index`). Missing, soft-deleted or another user's: the same `404`. No
`ETag`: the workspace token versions its metadata only, and each layout carries its own.
get.summary: Get a workspace with its layouts

put.description:
Full replacement of `WorkspaceInput` (an omitted field takes its default); layouts are
untouched and do not change this token. `409` and the 4 KiB limit as on `createWorkspace`.

`ETag` is the quoted token, `"<updated_at>"`, a strong validator. `If-Match` is optional
(absent: the last write wins) and takes that value; a `W/` prefix or the bare token is
accepted on input only, as leniency. Any other value, including `*` and a list of tags, is
unparseable.

Evaluation order for `/workspaces*` (not `exportWorkspace`, E15-S07) and `/layout-presets`
(steps that do not apply are skipped): `401`; `403` (permission, CSRF); `413`; `422` (path,
query, headers, body); `400 invalid_cursor` (lists); `Idempotency-Key` replay (stored 2xx +
`Idempotency-Replayed: true`) or `409 idempotency_key_reuse`; `404` (missing,
soft-deleted or another user's, identical); no-op `200` (the body changes nothing: unchanged
token, no write, even when `If-Match` is stale or unparseable, as the change is already
applied, RFC 9110 §13.1.1); `412 version_conflict` (stale or unparseable `If-Match`, nothing
written); `409`; the write. `503 store_unavailable` when storage fails.

get.description: The bundle is self-contained and contains no credentials, account identifiers or PnL figures - only presentation state - so it is safe to share. Import is `POST /workspaces` with `from_bundle`.
get.summary: Export a workspace as a portable bundle

get.description:
Live layouts (with all panes) of one of the caller's live workspaces, ordered by `id` (panes
by `slot_index`); at most 32. Missing, soft-deleted or another user's workspace: the same
`404`. `cursor` as on `listWorkspaces`, bound to this workspace.

400.description: Malformed request. For this operation `code: invalid_cursor` signals a malformed, foreign or expired `cursor`.

post.description:
A layout is a grid of up to 16 panes, persisted verbatim so the Electron shell restores the
exact arrangement. The server mints a UUIDv7 `id`; the pane set is validated as a whole and
written in the same transaction.

`422 validation_failed` lists up to 20 `errors[]`, naming a pane by array position (e.g.
`panes.2.slot_index`): rule `duplicate_slot`, the enums, the tree rules of `LayoutGridSpec`
(plus `grid_spec_required` for `custom` and `grid_spec_not_allowed` otherwise) and the pane
rules of `PaneKind`, `PaneConfig`, `PaneIntervalCode` and `LayoutPaneInput`. `409 conflict`:
rule `name_taken`, `hotkey_slot_taken`, `limit_reached` (32 live layouts) or
`concurrent_update`. `is_default: true` clears the previous default layout in the same
transaction. A workspace that is missing, soft-deleted or another user's returns the same
`404`.

Bodies over 128 KiB are refused with `413` (`payload_too_large`). The `ETag` header carries
the `updated_at` token. `Idempotency-Key` behaves as on `createWorkspace`.

value.detail: 1 field failed validation.

errors.message: slot_index 3 is already used by panes.0.

value.title: Request body or parameters failed schema validation

422.description: Semantically invalid layout. `code: validation_failed`; each entry of `errors[]` names the offending field, a pane by its array position.

get.description:
The layout with all of its panes (by `slot_index`). It must be live and belong to the named
workspace, one of the caller's live workspaces; otherwise the same `404`. The `ETag` header
carries the `updated_at` token.

put.description:
Called on pane rearrangement with a 2-second debounce. `If-Match` prevents a stale tab from
clobbering a newer arrangement made in another window.

Full replacement of the layout **and its whole pane set** in one transaction, validated as
on `createLayout` before anything is written; partial application is impossible. The
`updated_at` token versions the aggregate, so a pane-only change also changes it.
`If-Match`, the no-op rule and `412 version_conflict` work as on `updateWorkspace`; after a
`412` the stored layout is unchanged and the client re-reads it with `getLayout`. `404` as
on `getLayout`; `409`, `422` and the 128 KiB limit as on `createLayout`.
